summary: Madagascar's official eVisa portal says all nationalities are eligible for the tourist eVisa — a single-entry visa with a maximum duration of 60 days — and that the application can also be made on arrival at the eVisa counters, at the same prices. Fees depend on the length of stay: 1–15, 16–30 and 31–60 days.

notes: The UK FCDO says it is illegal to take any food, including fruit, into Madagascar. It says you may take out up to 2 kg of vanilla and up to 1 kg of pepper or cloves.
The UK FCDO says it is illegal to collect, buy or export protected animals, plants or products made from them, including items made of rosewood.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Madagascar has a cash-based economy: some credit cards are accepted at major hotels, some restaurants and shops, and cash can be withdrawn from a limited number of ATMs in Antananarivo. Euros are widely accepted and US dollars sometimes; ariary may not be exported.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says robberies and thefts are commonplace throughout Madagascar and that there have been violent robberies and assaults on isolated beaches, even in daytime. It advises avoiding political demonstrations and large gatherings, not walking alone in city centres or poorly lit areas after dark, and using pre-booked taxis or hotel transport.

tips.text: The UK FCDO says the cyclone season normally runs from November to April, with coastal areas particularly at risk; storms can cut access to remote parts of the country and contaminate water supplies.

Canada's travel advice says the military took over on 14 October 2025 after large-scale demonstrations and announced a two-year transition period. It says demonstrations are frequent and even peaceful ones can turn violent: avoid areas with demonstrations and large gatherings, and monitor local media.
Canada's travel advice says cash can be withdrawn from only a limited number of ATMs in Antananarivo and that some banks will not reconvert local currency into hard currency.

The UK FCDO says road conditions vary greatly and are often poor, advises against driving at night, and says many secondary roads are impassable except by 4-wheel-drive in the December–April rainy season. It also warns of armed robberies on main roads, particularly at night.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Madagascar?
faq.answer: Yes: Madagascar's eVisa portal says all nationalities are eligible for the eVisa, through which the tourist visa application is made online, and that the visa application can also be made on arrival at the eVisa counters. For the fees by length of stay, see the next question.

faq.question: How much does the Madagascar visa cost?
faq.answer: The eVisa portal's fee table lists EUR 30 (USD 35) for 1 to 15 days, EUR 35 (USD 41) for 16 to 30 days, EUR 40 (USD 47) for 31 to 60 days and EUR 50 (USD 59) for 61 to 90 days; the same portal says the tourist eVisa is a single-entry visa with a maximum duration of 60 days.

faq.question: Should I get the eVisa or a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: The official portal says the online prices are the same as those paid on arrival. The tourist eVisa is a single-entry visa with a maximum duration of 60 days; if you apply online (between one week and six months before departure), the electronic travel authorisation is issued within 72 hours and you present it at the eVisa counters on arrival. Otherwise you can make the application at those counters when you land.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Madagascar?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states whether a tourist eVisa can be extended. The official eVisa portal says the tourist eVisa is a single-entry visa with a maximum duration of 60 days.

faq.question: Is Madagascar safe to visit?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says petty crime is common throughout the country, that violent crime is reported in all regions, and that armed gangs have assaulted tourists in isolated areas such as beaches and national parks. Canada also says demonstrations are frequent and can turn violent, and the UK FCDO says the cyclone season normally runs from November to April.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Madagascar?
faq.answer: No official source we could read gives seasonal guidance for visitors. The UK FCDO says the cyclone season normally runs from November to April and that many secondary roads are impassable except by 4-wheel-drive in the December–April rainy season.

There are frequent armed robberies on main roads, particularly at night and outside major towns.
